findings.issue: The contract says that after commit the boundary 'sends status/body/allowed headers' and replays 'those bytes/status/headers'. It never says how an interceptor emits a non-default status in Nest 11, and the obvious way does not work. After the interceptor observable resolves, RouterExecutionContext.createHandleResponseFn (router-execution-context.js:192) calls ExpressAdapter.reply (express-adapter.js:45-46). reply runs response.status(httpStatusCode), and that value is the route's @HttpCode or the method default: 201 for POST, 200 otherwise. So calling res.status(502) and returning the body, which is the pattern the existing IdempotencyInterceptor.applyReplayHeaders uses (packages/idempotency/src/idempotency.interceptor.ts:195), puts the DELEGATION_FAILED body on the wire as 201/200. The same happens on a 502 replay. The other route is throwing after commit. The error then passes through consumer APP_FILTER exception filters and outer global interceptors such as SlaMonitorInterceptor (packages/backend/src/pipeline/platform-pipeline.module.ts:42). Those can reshape the body, so 'the exact body it sends' is not something the boundary controls. The contract also does not say what the client receives when a CommittedCommandError at an unselected status is rolled back.
findings.required_change: Pin one emission mechanism. Option A: after commit, the boundary throws an exported STYNX HttpException subclass (for example CommittedCommandResponse extends HttpException) carrying the stored status and body. The contract then states that the stored body is the exception payload and that exception filters must pass this type through unchanged, or explicitly documents which filter output is stored. Option B: the boundary writes the raw response and marks it handled. Define the replay path the same way. State the response for an unselected-status marker; a reasonable choice is that it rolls back and then surfaces as a normal HttpException with its status and body, with no key. Add Inspector cases through real Nest HTTP: a POST route with the default 201 whose committed 502 and its replay both carry wire status 502, and the same case with a consumer global exception filter and an outer response-mapping interceptor registered.

findings.issue: The wrapper is SECURITY DEFINER owned by stynx_owner, and stynx_owner is created BYPASSRLS (packages/data/migrations/platform/0001_roles.sql:4). Setting `row_security = on` on the function does not make policies apply to a BYPASSRLS role, so FORCE RLS on audit.events/audit.log does not apply inside the wrapper. Tenant correctness there depends only on the wrapper's own setting-derived tenant and audit.write's explicit `tenancy_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM p_tenant_id` filter (0008_audit.sql:204-210). audit.write also takes a free-text p_actor_role, which the wrapper would pass through from caller arguments. Also note that app.tenant_id/app.actor_id are custom settings stynx_app can itself change with set_config (database.ts:230-235). That is the same trust level as RLS, but it is not a stronger guarantee.
findings.required_change: Replace the 'retains FORCE RLS inside the definer / row_security=on' claim with: the wrapper enforces tenancy by its own validation. Derive actor_role from app.role or bound it to an enum. Document that the wrapper trusts the transaction-local settings to the same degree RLS does. Add a sensor showing the wrapper cannot write to a NULL-tenant or other-tenant chain even though the definer bypasses RLS.

findings.issue: 'Transaction-local lock timeout' set with SET LOCAL/set_config(...,true) stays in force for the rest of the command. That includes domain statements and audit.write's per-tenant `FOR UPDATE` on the chain head. Under the documented per-tenant serialization and external delegation latency, a 55P03 raised in the audit or domain step could be mapped to 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS, or could abort commands that are otherwise valid.
findings.required_change: Limit lockTimeoutMs to the reservation statement: set it, then restore the previous value. Map 55P03 to IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS only when it comes from the reservation step. A lock timeout anywhere else rolls back as an ordinary error. Add an Inspector case in which audit chain contention exceeds lockTimeoutMs and the response is not IN_PROGRESS.

findings.issue: 'Absent body is distinct from explicit JSON null' cannot be observed with default parsing. The default strict body-parser json rejects a top-level `null` with 400, and absent-body handling differs by Express major version (`{}` versus undefined). The fingerprint input is therefore ambiguous for bodyless POST and DELETE commands.
findings.required_change: Define absence by request framing (no Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding or zero length) rather than by the value of request.body. State that explicit null applies only when the consumer disables strict parsing. Add an Inspector case for a bodyless command under the default Nest 11 parser.

findings.issue: The predecessor gate is well defined: SHA, PASS receipt and integrated HEAD, all currently pending/blocked. But this contract already assumes predecessor semantics. It assumes RequestContext.actorId as the trusted default scope, a 'configured nominal or verified actor' for public routes, and CTG-0004's nested transaction constraints. None of those are frozen yet. If CTG-0003 or CTG-0004 freeze a different surface, this contract could be dispatched without anyone reconciling the difference.
findings.required_change: Add a gate row condition: after the predecessors are integrated, the Architect confirms or amends the actor, public-scope and nested-transaction assumptions against the frozen CTG-0003/0004 contracts. Any amendment requires a new cross-family prompt review before Inspector dispatch.

summary: All five cycle-1 blockers are closed against STYNX source. (1) CommittedCommandError is the sole committed-terminal marker; it is caught inside Database.tx, appends one audit event, and a plain thrown HttpException(502) rolls back with no key. (2) The symbols and packages are pinned: TransactionalCommand, the module and interceptor, the @Idempotent/@Audit transactional overloads, and TxOptions.requireActor. One APP_INTERCEPTOR boundary owns the ordering, fails closed before next.handle(), and uses retry:false, which the red suite verifies as a single handler run on 40001. (3) Migration 0020 adds a restricted SECURITY DEFINER audit.write_command_event that reads tenant/actor from app.* settings, alongside a TransactionalAuditSink port. Backend adds the data/audit dependencies, which introduces no cycle. The owned paths are extended, and a real stynx_app PostgreSQL proof is required. (4) Identity is tenant+scope+key, with a concrete-path fingerprint, a 409 envelope and NULL-tenant isolation. (5) The CTG-0003/0004 SHA/PASS/HEAD gate is explicit, and prompts 60, 61 and 62 are blocked on it. UPS-TXN-01…05 are all covered as MUST under OD-S15-01. One blocking gap remains: the contract does not say how the boundary emits the committed or replayed non-default status. Nest overwrites a status set in an interceptor with the @HttpCode or method default (201/200), and exception filters and outer interceptors can reshape the body, so the committed 502 and the exact replay are underspecified. After that is repaired, the contract and prompts would qualify for a conditional PASS. Even then, Inspector dispatch stays blocked until the predecessor rows are recorded.
